items.text: Products in $C[\Sigma'^{-1}]$
Given a family $Y\to X_i$ of dotted arrows; to factor it through $X=\prod X_i$ (in $C$).
Y \dashrightarrow X_i \;=\; (Z_i \to Y)\in\Sigma' \ \text{ with } \ Z_i\to X_i
Z=\prod_{i,\,Y} Z_i \longrightarrow Y \ \in\ \Sigma' \qquad\text{(property 4)}
One $Z\to Y$ in $\Sigma'$; every $Z\to X_i$ factors through it, so $Z\to X$ exists ($X$ a product in $C$).
Existence of the factorisation: done.
Uniqueness
Two dotted arrows $Y\to X$ with the same components $p_i$.
After replacing $Y$ by $Y'\to Y$ in $\Sigma'$: both are honest arrows $Y\to X$.
$Y'\to Y$ is invertible in $C[\Sigma'^{-1}]$, so take $Y'=Y$.
K_i=\ker(p_i f,\,p_i g)\hookrightarrow Y \ \in\ \Sigma' \qquad K=\bigcap_i K_i=\textstyle\prod_Y K_i
$K\to Y$ is in $\Sigma'$; $f|_K=g|_K$, hence $f=g$ as dotted arrows.
So $C\to C[\Sigma'^{-1}]$ commutes with products.
Remark: localisation within $\Delta$
Surjective on objects: no new objects, only new arrows between constructions.
Strictly cogenerating subcategories
$I\to\widetilde I$ (adding inverse limits): fully faithful, and $\mathrm{Ob}\,I$ cogenerates $\widetilde I$.
Dually, $J\subset\widehat J$ is a set of generators: every object of $\widehat J$ is a direct limit of objects of $J$.
\text{every } X\in\widehat J:\quad X=\varinjlim_{J_{/X}} j \qquad(J\ \text{strictly generating})
Five or six variants of « generating »; for topoi (or exactness conditions) they coincide, for categories not.
I\ \text{strictly cogenerating in } \widetilde I:\quad X=\varprojlim_{X\to i} i
Problem 2 and passage to the limit
$C\mapsto C[\Sigma^{-1}]$: same objects, so $I$ stays strictly cogenerating.
R_\alpha\ \text{ in }\Delta\ \text{(filtering)},\quad I\to R_\alpha\ \text{strictly cogenerating}\ \Longrightarrow\ I\to R=\varinjlim R_\alpha\ \text{too}
Checked « modulo mistakes ».
Adding arrows
R\longrightarrow R_H \ \text{(in }\Delta),\qquad I\to R \ \text{strictly cogenerating}
Claim: $I$ is strictly cogenerating in $R_H$. « Strictly » is transitive; it suffices that $R$ is.
Step 1: add arrows, formal composites: same objects.
Step 2: envelope with respect to $\Delta$: the original objects still cogenerate.
Step 3: make arrows invertible, $C\Sigma^{-1}$ in $\Delta$: same objects.
In all four steps of building a theory from $I$, $I$ stays strictly cogenerating.
Theorem (semantics of algebraic theories of type $\Delta$)
The algebraic theories are those represented by categories $R$ in $\Delta$ (arbitrary inverse limits) with a small strictly cogenerating subcategory.
I\to R \text{ basic}\iff I \text{ is strictly cogenerating in } R
A conjecture in general: here a theorem.
Dually: categories with arbitrary direct limits and a small strictly generating set.
Converse
Done: a theory has the property. Remaining: given $I\to R$ with the property, it is a theory.
I'=\text{full subcategory of } R \text{ on } \mathrm{Ob}\,I,\qquad I\to I'\to R
T_{\widetilde{I'}}\colon C\mapsto \underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_{\mathrm{Cat}}(I',C)=\underline{\mathrm{Hom}}_\Delta(\widetilde{I'},C)
An algebraic theory in three steps: (a) empty structure on the objects, (b) add the arrows of $I'$, (c) axioms (associativity).
T_R\longrightarrow T_{\widetilde{I'}}
Claim: $R$ is a category of fractions of $\widetilde{I'}$.
\widetilde{I'}\longrightarrow R \ \text{ essentially surjective on objects}
Each object of $R$ is the limit of a diagram in $I'$ (full), which has a limit in $\widetilde{I'}$.
On arrows: $f\colon X\to Y$ in $R$ gives a functor between categories of objects under:
Y\backslash I'\longrightarrow X\backslash I',\qquad X=\varprojlim_{X\backslash I'} i,\quad Y=\varprojlim_{Y\backslash I'} i
So $f$ comes from a morphism of canonical inverse systems, hence from $\widetilde{I'}$.
$R$ is a quotient of $\widetilde{I'}$; the functor is left exact, so only isomorphisms need be imposed.
Count: void structure on $I$; add arrows; equate composites; equate arrows. The last two merge: no transfinite construction.

Realizations in sets
S=\text{realizations of } T \text{ in } \mathbf{Sets},\qquad T(C)=\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta(R,C)
Functors $R\to\mathbf{Sets}$ commuting with inverse limits are representable:
T(\mathbf{Sets})=R^{\circ}\ \Longrightarrow\ R\simeq S^{\circ}
The realizations in sets determine the whole theory: $R$ is the opposite of $S$.
In $S^\circ$ for groups there is a canonical group (a cogroup); for rings, a co-ring.

C\ \subset\ \langle C\rangle_{D'}\ \subset\ \bar C\qquad(\text{closure of } C \text{ under } D'\text{-limits in } \bar C)
